Pure Nostalgia and a Masterpiece of Gaming History!

I bought Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition because I’ve known this game for as long as I can remember. When I was a little kid, I used to sit right behind my dad and just watch him play :) Having it now brings back the ultimate nostalgia, and it's just a wonderful feeling.

I haven't spent an endless amount of time in it, but I'm completely fine with that. Campaigns were never really my thing, but jumping into a quick match and trying out all the different civilizations is always a blast. With so many different maps and game modes, it's a true piece of computer history.

Look. I know pointing to my playtime and walking away is lazy, but like...what more do you want from me? It's the 1999 classic in all its glory but with a support level on par with any modern game. You can reasonably criticize the idea to upend certain long-standing gameplay systems with more recent patches and expansions, but at its core it still hits all the nostalgia notes while also allowing the growth that comes from 25+ years of game and map design evolution. And some of the newer, longer story campaigns from Chronicles or the recent Viking Sagas show that the underlying engine can power vastly different ideas than whatever was envisioned back then.

Like, I can play a complicated, 12-hour scenario full of triggers and conditions, with all the polish of a major studio, but I can also still play basically the same scenarios I played on my Pentium III when I was 15. Or I can just comp-stomp and vibe to the soundtrack. More than any of the other Definitive Editions, it's a platform for both memories and modern development.
